attributes.residual: real 16, insns 66/66, opcode multiset IDENTICAL but the residual is SCHEDULE, not REGISTER_ONLY, and that distinction is the whole finding. ONE NAMED MECHANISM: the loop-invariant shift mask's literal 1 is materialised on the WRONG SIDE of the counted-loop setup. Target emits `li r0,4; lwz r4,224(r3); mtctr r0; li r0,1; lis r3,gPlayers@ha; slw r6,r0,r4` -- it spends r0 on the trip count, hands it to mtctr, and then RECYCLES the freed r0 for the constant 1. Ours emits `li r0,4; lwz r4,224(r3); li r5,1; mtctr r0; ...; slw r6,r5,r4` -- the constant is materialised BEFORE mtctr, while r0 is still live with the trip count, so it must take a fresh register (r5). That single placement choice cascades to the rest of the residual: with r5 consumed by the constant, ours colours the gPlayers base r5 and the loop byte offset r3, where target (with r5 free) colours them r4 and r5, and the in-loop mulli temp lands in r4 instead of target's r3. So all 16 real lines follow from one instruction's position. This is why the WebFrank path is unavailable: the difference is an instruction REORDER, not a register-field edit, and tools/gdl/webfrank_audit.py accordingly classifies only TowerCheckMessages (not this function) as register-only in this TU.
